elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: § 8.2 as rendered still provides automatic renewal ("Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives sixty (60) days' advance written notice"), not renewal by mutual written agreement, and the conditional automatic-renewal elements are not all satisfied (opt-out window is 60 rather than 30 days, and no Vendor reminder obligation exists). To reach preferred, either convert § 8.2 to renewal only on the Parties' mutual written agreement, or shorten Customer's notice to 30 days and add an express Vendor reminder at least 60 days before each renewal.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: § 8.2: "Each Order Form renews for twelve months" — a single 12-month renewal term, at the ceiling and not a multi-year renewal.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Renewal is automatic, so the condition applies. § 8.2 as rendered requires "sixty (60) days' advance written notice" to prevent renewal, which exceeds the 30-day preferred ceiling. Repair by changing the notice figure in § 8.2 to thirty (30) days.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: Renewal is automatic, so the condition applies. Neither § 8.2 nor § 8.3 contains any renewal-reminder obligation; § 8.3's ninety-day notice runs only to a Fee increase, not to renewal itself. Repair by inserting an express obligation on Vendor to notify Customer of the upcoming renewal at least 60 days before the renewal date.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: § 8.3 (retained unchanged): "Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent."

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 8.2 replaces "one hundred eighty days" with "sixty (60) days' advance written notice," and the window runs to "either Party," so Customer's non-renewal notice window is exactly 60 days — at, not above, the fallback ceiling.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: § 8.3 caps renewal uplift at "the lesser of" CPI and "three percent," which is necessarily ≤ 5 percent; already met without edit.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the single edit brings the non-renewal window to exactly 60 days, and the retained § 8.3 cap (lesser of CPI and 3%) is inside the 5% fallback ceiling.

Preferred is not reached: the window is 60 rather than 30 days and there is no Vendor renewal-reminder obligation at least 60 days before renewal; these are noted as short of preferred, consistent with the rationale.

Minimal: the only textual change is the numeral in § 8.2 (180 days → sixty (60) days). The 12-month renewal term, the mutual 'either Party' structure, and all of § 8.3 (CPI/3% cap, 90-day increase notice, no increase on prepaid periods) are retained verbatim; no survival tails, procedures, or extra requirements were added.

Preserves intent: the renewal mechanic, Order Form references, defined terms (Order Form, Fees) and pricing/notice timing elsewhere are untouched; no dangling cross-reference, undefined trigger, or contradictory retained sentence results. Non-renewal here is natural-term expiry and is correctly evaluated under RENEWAL rather than as a convenience-termination right.
Deviation classification is sound: the original 180-day window exceeded both the 60-day fallback ceiling and the 90-day walk-away threshold, so a redline was warranted rather than a rationale note.
